## T1: Keying slip: a record filed under an ID it does not belong to

- **Status:** proven
- **Family:** record_reversal
- **Aimed at:** both
- **Clock trap:** no
- **Aliases:** ID.slip, keying slip, governing_vs_filing_key
- **Pooled misses:** Fable 742/1835 (40%), Astra 602/1490 (40%)
- **Loopholes:** L-record, L-join, L-union, L-threshold

A structured record (export row, log entry, filed note) carries an ID that is not its owner's. The default joins on the printed key and prices, counts or routes the record under that ID. The files make that impossible: two or more first-hand remarks from different parties describe the record's content, and only the true owner fits. Fable usually notices the conflict and keeps the record anyway; Astra joins silently. Measured here (build_evidence.py, 2026-10-15): final 10x2 pooled Fable 345/680, Astra 321/670; all stages Fable 742/1835, Astra 602/1490 (AMBIGUOUS/DEFECT units excluded); without unaudited >=90% units, final Fable 297/610, Astra 257/580. Audited GENUINE in 13 task(s). Status proven: audited GENUINE in 13 tasks; pooled final miss rate >= 0.2 with n >= 20 on fable, astra (unaudited >= 90% units excluded).

**Recipe**

- *record:* an official-looking keyed record (export row, dispatch line, inbox row) whose own content fits its printed key well enough to pass a casual check
- *anchors:* two or more by-the-way remarks from different parties, each in a document read for another purpose, that describe the record's content and fit only the true owner; at least one makes the printed owner impossible (a date, a location, a transfer)
- *withheld:* no sentence gives the key or record priority, and no sentence names the mechanism of the slip (no 'typo', no 'page-number slip'); the solver supplies the mechanism
- *dials:*
  - one by-the-way anchor per notch toward solvable (a witness of the event or a unique content match)
  - for Astra change the KIND of evidence, not the amount
  - never add a descriptor only the true owner has: it flips the bite to 0
- *conservation:* when the record could be credited to both IDs, grade both sides against a conserved total so the union answer loses
- *shields:* if a tempting rule exists, scope it away from the keyed variable explicitly

**Proof obligations (authoring/validate.py)**

- uniqueness: solve.py enumerates the candidate owners and exactly one fits every anchor
- ablation: dropping each anchor leaves the owner underdetermined or the default (executed)
- no-priority grep: no fixture sentence binds the printed key (audits withdrew psychopathy 2.1.0, ktp 2.1.0, cafe 2.1.0 for one)
- additivity: the keyed reading fails exactly this premise's checks (design_lint)
- blind reader before any dial when a model misses 5/5

**Hazards**

- a sentence that blesses the record makes it AMBIGUOUS: psychopathy 2.1.0 P4 ('the log decides'), ktp 2.1.0 P2 ('the class journal records each lesson'), cafe 2.1.0 P10 (clause 2.2 'drawings govern')
- two records that conflict symmetrically with nothing to decide between them: coloring 2.2.0 P2/P5/P8 AMBIGUOUS, fixed by one first-hand remark in 2.3.0
- a column whose provenance is unstated while a rule defers to it: probation 2.2.0 P4 (AMBIGUOUS, re-audit UNCLEAR)
- a later dated note that supports the printed label: feast 1.1.0 P3 AMBIGUOUS
- a graded label that exists in no file: line-colour 1.0.0 P2 DEFECT
- a 'credit both' reading left open when nothing makes the printed owner impossible: ats 1.1.0 and 1.6.0 P2, closed by an impossibility anchor in 1.7.0
- often flat: 10 of the 19 audited units in the 45-task pass were missed at least 90% by Fable (kibo P3, pathway P2, ats P2, suitcase P5)

**What killed it**

- one descriptor only the true owner has: cnc 2.4.0/2.5.0 P3 'still coiled, wire-tied' took 15/15 to 0/5 on both models
- a specific first-hand noun: coloring 2.4.0/2.5.0 'little crow' took Fable to 2/15, 4/15, 0/15
- a new note placed beside the anchor primes a destination check: gst 1.5.0 P1 11/15 to 0/5 with byte-identical premise text
- one origin remark: gst 1.5.0 P4 'lorry up from Hubballi' 13/15 to 0/5
- kibo 2.8.0 P3 dial (hand-typed name route) overshot to 0/5 on both

**Trace signals**

- the user corrects which file, row, ID or person an item belongs to
- two lists keyed by IDs that are easy to transpose (adjacent register lines, consecutive slide or order numbers)
- a record built by someone other than the people who saw the event (data entry from paper slips, an export of hand-typed names)

**Domains**

- school registers and option slips
- procurement and goods received
- applicant tracking
- production logs and art boards
- small-business bookkeeping

**Example.** An export row keyed to a learner who transferred out three days before slips were collected carries a combination that the homeroom teacher's note and a club leader's remark both tie to a classmate whose slip is missing from the export.

## T2: Convention fixed only by worked figures in the governing document

- **Status:** promising
- **Family:** convention_inference
- **Aimed at:** both
- **Clock trap:** no
- **Aliases:** CV.round, CV.method, convention from worked figures
- **Pooled misses:** Fable 439/2670 (16%), Astra 252/2065 (12%)
- **Loopholes:** L-default, L-absorb, L-shield

The governing text states what to compute but not how to round, count or bound it; only its worked figures (or a filed record of the same procedure) fix the convention: truncate vs half-up, which end of a range, whether the arrival day counts. The default applies the ordinary convention (round(), half-up, plain mean). This mode now covers every convention set by worked figures, as authors template it; rounding and truncation are its strongest sub-shape. Measured here (build_evidence.py, 2026-10-15): final 10x2 pooled Fable 185/970, Astra 129/950; all stages Fable 439/2670, Astra 252/2065 (AMBIGUOUS/DEFECT units excluded); without unaudited >=90% units, final Fable 137/920, Astra 114/900. Audited GENUINE in 10 task(s). Status promising: short of proven: no model with pooled final rate >= 0.2 at n >= 20; not dead (some model above 0.05 or n < 20).

**Recipe**

- *record:* the governing rule states the quantity and its precision but not the convention
- *anchors:* worked figures in the governing document itself, or in a same-procedure filed record the rule points to; for Astra exactly one discriminating figure outside the entry that defines the graded rate
- *withheld:* no sentence names the convention ('truncate', 'cut', 'count the arrival day')
- *dials:*
  - the number and placement of discriminating figures: one figure gave Astra about 100% in several builds; two gave anywhere from 3/15 to 14/15
  - a figure inside the entry that defines the graded rate kills it for Astra
  - keep non-discriminating figures (both conventions agree) as cover
- *conservation:* graded figures must discriminate under every upstream answer the solver could give (grade on the solver's own list)
- *shields:* the task's own other content must not act as a competing example set, or the audit must show it is not governing (deck titles)

**Proof obligations (authoring/validate.py)**

- discrimination: solve.py shows each plausible convention fails at least one worked figure, and exactly one fits all
- placement: every worked figure sits in the governing text or a same-module filed record (eco-guard 2.1.0 fix)
- additivity: the default convention fails exactly this premise's checks
- census: deliverables diffed against the reference to separate convention misses from cascades

**Hazards**

- worked figures in documents the rule does not govern make it AMBIGUOUS: eco-guard 2.1.0 P3 (sheets from another year and module), brightwater 1.3.0 P3 ('within' promises outside the site-promise rule)
- the idiom 'to one decimal place' reads as ordinary rounding: profile 2.1.0-2.4.0 P5 shipped GENUINE-soft
- one discriminating figure is GENUINE-soft at best: deck 2.8.0 P4, gst 1.7.0 P2
- a cascade from an upstream answer graded against the reference: gst 1.3.0 P2 DEFECT (convention missed 0/30 once fixed)
- a token nobody can settle (a spaced em dash counted or not as a word): moot 2.1.0 P10 AMBIGUOUS
- a competing example set inside the task (the deck's own v3 titles cited as precedent): deck 2.3.0 and 2.8.0 disclosures

**What killed it**

- a worked figure inside the entry that defines the graded rate: profile 2.5.0 P5 Astra 14/15 to 0/5, never recovered in 2.6-2.8
- figures one division away from the graded case: coloring spine 0/30 in every form
- a stated precedent clause: kibo 2.1.0 P4 (5/5 to 0/5)
- one figure for Fable: 18/200 misses in the 45-task pass

**Trace signals**

- the user corrects a rounding or a count the assistant computed
- a style guide or procedure with examples but no explicit rounding rule
- filed earlier reports that show the house convention

**Domains**

- financial reporting and board decks
- tax workbooks
- survey and lab results sheets
- service charters
- publishing specifications

**Example.** A house style gives figures over one million in millions with one decimal; its one discriminating worked example shows 2,480,000 as 2.4 million (half-up would give 2.5), so the graded figures must be cut, not rounded.

## T3: Quantity basis cued only on or about the record (tax-inclusive, per pack)

- **Status:** proven
- **Family:** quantity_basis
- **Aimed at:** both
- **Clock trap:** no
- **Aliases:** Q.taxincl, Q.pack, quantity basis
- **Pooled misses:** Fable 153/235 (65%), Astra 49/200 (24%)
- **Loopholes:** L-default, L-shield, L-threshold

A price or quantity is read on the wrong basis: a tax-inclusive bill read as net, a price per pair or pack read as per piece. The basis is cued only on or about the record itself (a cheque note, a received-goods tally, the seller's filed orders), never in a caption next to the figures. Fable misses tax-inclusive bases; per-pack pricing with a tally bites both. Measured here (build_evidence.py, 2026-10-15): final 10x2 pooled Fable 78/90, Astra 23/90; all stages Fable 153/235, Astra 49/200 (AMBIGUOUS/DEFECT units excluded). Audited GENUINE in 4 task(s). Status proven: audited GENUINE in 4 tasks; pooled final miss rate >= 0.2 with n >= 20 on fable, astra (unaudited >= 90% units excluded).

**Recipe**

- *record:* a bill, list price or order line whose figures look complete on the default basis
- *anchors:* a cue on the record or about this record (a tally of what was received, the seller's own filed order lines, a remark that the rise was not passed on)
- *withheld:* no caption or column header states the basis
- *dials:*
  - change the kind of evidence (a received-goods tally moved Astra where more filed lists of the same kind did not: cnc 2.6.0 P4)
  - the weakest oblique cue restored the Fable bite on gst P3 ('same rates as our counter board')
- *conservation:* the per-piece reading must contradict a received count or a total
- *shields:* a 'printed rate governs' rule must be scoped to rates, not to what the price includes

**Proof obligations (authoring/validate.py)**

- uniqueness: only one basis reproduces the tally or the paid total
- ablation: without the on-record cue the basis is underdetermined (executed)
- blind reader: a non-governing-document cue that the reader also misses is unfair

**Hazards**

- a cue in a caption next to the figures is a stated rule: suitcase 2.2.0/2.3.0 P7 Fable 0/10
- a cue only in a non-governing document with one out-of-population figure: suitcase 2.4.0/2.5.0 P7, blind reader also missed (UNCONFIRMED)
- a single route is GENUINE-soft: cnc 2.3.0 P4
- bimodal by model: tax-inclusive bit Fable 33/40 finals and Astra 0/40 (gst P3)

**What killed it**

- one extra cue on every line: gst 1.5.0/1.6.0 P3 10/15 to 1/5 and 0/5 ('a single figure on each line', a second 'nothing to add on' note)
- student P3 tax-exclusive quote: 0/15 F, 0/10 A

**Trace signals**

- the user corrects a total because a price already included tax or covered two items
- receipts or tallies that disagree with list prices
- retail or workshop purchasing

**Domains**

- small retail and stationery
- workshop and maker BOMs
- trading-card and hobby budgets
- merchandising price matrices

**Example.** A bearing listed at one price per line is ordered one per piece, though the seller's own filed orders and the receiving tally show each line delivered two pieces.

## T4: Already in hand: a 'still needed' item already held, shown by a technical bridge

- **Status:** promising
- **Family:** possession_state
- **Aimed at:** both
- **Clock trap:** no
- **Aliases:** S.inhand, already in hand
- **Pooled misses:** Fable 24/165 (15%), Astra 13/145 (9%)
- **Loopholes:** L-record, L-threshold

A rule orders or chases what is still needed, and a list says an item is outstanding. A first-hand record shows the item is already held, through a technical bridge the solver must make (a controller already running a known board; a vendor's job sheet for the scanned specimen). The default orders or chases the item. It dies when possession is stated. Measured here (build_evidence.py, 2026-10-15): final 10x2 pooled Fable 13/70, Astra 8/70; all stages Fable 24/165, Astra 13/145 (AMBIGUOUS/DEFECT units excluded). Audited GENUINE in 2 task(s). Status promising: short of proven: no model with pooled final rate >= 0.2 at n >= 20; not dead (some model above 0.05 or n < 20).

**Recipe**

- *record:* a still-needed list or chase line that names the item as outstanding
- *anchors:* two first-hand records whose technical content shows the item is held (a log line, a job sheet, an adviser's identification of the object)
- *withheld:* no sentence says the item arrived or is owned
- *dials:*
  - one semantic bridge per notch; two bridges were disclosed as the soft point in cnc 2.6.0
- *conservation:* grade the order or chase list as an exact set
- *shields:* scope any 'chase everything on the list' rule to items not yet received

**Proof obligations (authoring/validate.py)**

- uniqueness: exactly one listed item is shown held
- ablation: each bridge anchor is necessary (executed)
- no-statement grep: no line states possession

**Hazards**

- two semantic bridges were disclosed as the soft point: cnc 2.6.0 P5
- measured on two tasks only: cnc P5 (Fable) and psychopathy 2.4.0 P6 (Astra, templated T4 by its author)

**What killed it**

- possession stated outright: kibo 2.5.0/2.6.0 P5 commander scope, Fable 0/10
- possession inferred from one incidental remark: kibo 2.7.0 P5 0/5; blockprint P2 stock in the lock-up 0/10
- brightwater 1.4.0-1.6.0 P5 (T4 build): Fable 0/20 finals

**Trace signals**

- the user says 'I already have that' after a list is drafted
- shopping or procurement lists built from a template
- equipment or documents arriving by a side channel

**Domains**

- maker and workshop builds
- research data management
- web content launches
- budget card builds

**Example.** A build list still orders a controller kit, though the printer log shows the owner's own board already running the matching firmware on all four axes.

## T5: Misfiled note or record: filed under one item, content only fits another

- **Status:** proven
- **Family:** record_reversal
- **Aimed at:** both
- **Clock trap:** no
- **Aliases:** misfiled note
- **Pooled misses:** Fable 53/170 (31%), Astra 81/170 (48%)
- **Loopholes:** L-record, L-absorb, L-threshold

A note, comment, letter or certificate is filed under item A, but what it says can only be about item B (dates, details or a description that A cannot meet). The default applies it to A as filed. Content-only misfiles bit Astra hard in some builds (ats, pathway) and not at all in others (spice 2.5.0, line-colour 1.4.0, timesheet 2.7.0). Measured here (build_evidence.py, 2026-10-15): final 10x2 pooled Fable 26/80, Astra 41/80; all stages Fable 53/170, Astra 81/170 (AMBIGUOUS/DEFECT units excluded); without unaudited >=90% units, final Fable 26/60, Astra 21/60. Audited GENUINE in 2 task(s). Status proven: audited GENUINE in 2 tasks; pooled final miss rate >= 0.2 with n >= 20 on fable, astra (unaudited >= 90% units excluded).

**Recipe**

- *record:* a complete note or comment that fits its filed key on a casual read
- *anchors:* two near-true details in the note that A cannot meet and B does (a date offset, a prior history), each checked against a record read for another purpose
- *withheld:* no sentence says the note was misfiled
- *dials:*
  - two near-true details: the ats 1.6.0 reader solved it, models still missed
  - an impossibility on A closes the 'apply to both' reading
- *conservation:* grade both A's and B's resulting values so 'apply to both' loses
- *shields:* none needed unless a filing rule exists; then scope it

**Proof obligations (authoring/validate.py)**

- uniqueness: only B meets every detail of the note
- ablation: each detail is necessary
- both-side grading: the union answer fails a check

**Hazards**

- an instruction-like note admitting a second destination: deck 2.5.0 N5 AMBIGUOUS (fixed 2.6.0)
- a one-day relayed count plus one likelihood is the thinnest point the audit accepted: ats 1.7.0 P6
- flat when it bites: ats 1.7.0 P6 was 20/20 the same wrong value

**What killed it**

- timesheet 2.7.0 P6 IT-log note: 0/15 on both models
- spice 2.5.0 P7 and line-colour 1.4.0 P5: 0/5 on both

**Trace signals**

- the user says a comment or attachment belongs to another item
- comment exports, certificate logs and correspondence filed by subject line

**Domains**

- recruiting and HR registers
- school administration
- deck and document review
- trading journals

**Example.** A resignation note filed under one candidate says notice was served 'three days after sitting our paper', which fits only the other candidate's sitting date.

## T6: Which edition or rate applies, by the real date (sources of similar authority)

- **Status:** promising
- **Family:** authority_selection
- **Aimed at:** both
- **Clock trap:** no
- **Aliases:** T.edition, version_in_force
- **Pooled misses:** Fable 96/245 (39%), Astra 113/140 (81%)
- **Loopholes:** L-record, L-shield

Two editions, briefs or rates could govern; the log's key or date points to one, and first-hand dated records show the request really arrived under the other. The default trusts the log's date or the newest edition. It bites both models when the competing sources have similar authority; it is unfair when an informal remark contradicts an official printed form. Measured here (build_evidence.py, 2026-10-15): final 10x2 pooled Fable 50/80, Astra 78/90; all stages Fable 96/245, Astra 113/140 (AMBIGUOUS/DEFECT units excluded); without unaudited >=90% units, final Fable 50/80, Astra 59/70. Audited GENUINE in 1 task(s). Status promising: short of proven: audited GENUINE in 1 task(s) (< 2); not dead (some model above 0.05 or n < 20).

**Recipe**

- *record:* a log or register that keys the job to an edition by its entry date
- *anchors:* first-hand dated records (a fitting date, a recording made on a named day) that place the real receipt in the other edition's window
- *withheld:* no mapping rule from date to edition is stated
- *dials:*
  - one oblique sentence moved cafe P1/P6 into the band on Fable ('on Thursday')
- *conservation:* the wrong edition must flip at least one graded verdict
- *shields:* never let a printed current form state the opposite of the answer

**Proof obligations (authoring/validate.py)**

- authority parity: the competing sources are of similar standing (audit)
- uniqueness: the dated records fit only one edition window
- blind reader: if the reader misses it too, treat as unfair

**Hazards**

- an informal remark against an official printed form is unfair: home-bp 2.6.0/2.7.0 P5, blind reader also missed (UNCONFIRMED)
- the first blind reader missed the edition question (cafe 2.1.0: 0.78); a second reached it
- re-decided in a fresh step it is a constant lever charged twice (cafe P1/P6 disclosure)
- one audited task only (cafe)

**What killed it**

- a stated mapping rule: timesheet 2.4.0-2.6.0 P5 payroll period 0/25
- a stated reprint date: home-bp 2.4.0/2.5.0 P5 Fable 0/10

**Trace signals**

- the user names which version of a brief, standard or rate card applies
- revisions issued while the job was in progress

**Domains**

- fit-out and kitchen design
- payroll and rate cards
- clinical protocols
- legal and regulatory editions

**Example.** A design brief logged on an early date is in fact the later request, because it mentions a frame fitted a week after that date and a recording the client made on the new day.

## T7: Convention from two worked figures supplied by different parties

- **Status:** promising
- **Family:** convention_inference
- **Aimed at:** fable
- **Clock trap:** no
- **Aliases:** two-party worked figures
- **Pooled misses:** Fable 16/55 (29%), Astra 7/55 (13%)
- **Loopholes:** L-default, L-absorb

A convention (build at the floor, not at the nominal height) is shown by two worked figures from two different parties, one in a standard and one in a client's filed request. The default applies the nominal reading. Measured on one task only. Measured here (build_evidence.py, 2026-10-15): final 10x2 pooled Fable 9/30, Astra 4/40; all stages Fable 16/55, Astra 7/55 (AMBIGUOUS/DEFECT units excluded). Audited GENUINE in 1 task(s). Status promising: short of proven: audited GENUINE in 1 task(s) (< 2); not dead (some model above 0.05 or n < 20).

**Recipe**

- *record:* a nominal figure the default uses directly
- *anchors:* two worked cases from different parties that fit only the convention
- *withheld:* the convention is never stated
- *dials:*
  - a third figure moves it toward solvable
- *conservation:* graded values must differ under the two conventions
- *shields:* scope any 'nominal heights govern' sentence

**Proof obligations (authoring/validate.py)**

- discrimination: each worked figure fails the default
- placement: both figures in documents that govern the build

**Hazards**

- within-premise double charges were disclosed in the cafe 2.1.1 audit
- one task only (cafe P11)

**Trace signals**

- the user corrects a height or size by pointing at an earlier job

**Domains**

- fit-out and joinery
- engineering drawings

**Example.** A rack height follows the floor build, as both a standard's worked case and a client's earlier request show, rather than the nominal worktop height.

## T8: Changed premise received before issue (filler only)

- **Status:** promising
- **Family:** revision_supersession
- **Aimed at:** fable
- **Clock trap:** no
- **Aliases:** changed premise before issue
- **Pooled misses:** Fable 12/55 (22%), Astra 0/55 (0%)
- **Loopholes:** L-record, L-shield

A letter received before the issue date changes a premise (a door must stay an escape door), so verdicts computed on the old premise are wrong. The default keeps the earlier verdicts. Measured on one task; the catalogue keeps it as a filler. Measured here (build_evidence.py, 2026-10-15): final 10x2 pooled Fable 7/30, Astra 0/40; all stages Fable 12/55, Astra 0/55 (AMBIGUOUS/DEFECT units excluded). Audited GENUINE in 1 task(s). Status promising: short of proven: audited GENUINE in 1 task(s) (< 2); not dead (some model above 0.05 or n < 20).

**Recipe**

- *record:* verdicts already worked out on the old premise
- *anchors:* a dated letter received before the issue and a drawing that ties it to the graded items
- *withheld:* no instruction says to re-check
- *dials:*
- *conservation:* the changed premise must flip graded verdicts
- *shields:* scope the PM's 'the change is X' sentence to its paragraph

**Proof obligations (authoring/validate.py)**

- dates: the change is received before the issue (executed)
- additivity: the old premise fails exactly this check

**Hazards**

- one task only (cafe P8)

**What killed it**

- every other changed-premise build is dead (see D14)

**Trace signals**

- the user forwards a late letter that changes a requirement

**Domains**

- fit-out
- building control

**Example.** A civil-protection letter received the day before issue makes one door an escape route, so two units that pass clearance against the old swing now fail.

## T9: Rule-scope shield: a real rule on a neighbouring value over-applied

- **Status:** promising
- **Family:** rule_scope
- **Aimed at:** fable
- **Clock trap:** no
- **Aliases:** rule-scope shield, L-shield
- **Pooled misses:** Fable 55/120 (46%), Astra 4/120 (3%)
- **Loopholes:** L-shield, L-threshold

A real rule governs a neighbouring value (a guide section that leaves late sitters out of the gain); the default over-applies it to the graded value (it also leaves their pre-test out). Three or more lines show the graded value stands. Fable cites the rule; Astra rarely misses. Measured here (build_evidence.py, 2026-10-15): final 10x2 pooled Fable 32/60, Astra 3/60; all stages Fable 55/120, Astra 4/120 (AMBIGUOUS/DEFECT units excluded). Audited GENUINE in 1 task(s). Status promising: short of proven: audited GENUINE in 1 task(s) (< 2); not dead (some model above 0.05 or n < 20).

**Recipe**

- *record:* a governing section whose rule is about a neighbouring value
- *anchors:* three or more lines (handover, record sheet, instruction) that treat the graded value as recorded
- *withheld:* no clarification that the rule covers only the neighbouring value
- *dials:*
  - each additional line that uses the graded value is one notch toward solvable
- *conservation:* grade the graded value and the neighbouring value separately
- *shields:* the shield is the trap: the audit must show the rule's grammar does not reach the graded value

**Proof obligations (authoring/validate.py)**

- scope proof: the audit quotes the rule and shows it does not reach the graded value
- three supporting lines present (grep)
- blind reader

**Hazards**

- the first audit called the melody 1.1.0 bite AMBIGUOUS; the B7 re-audit found the rule's own scope defeats the null reading (melody 1.1.0, re-audit TOO STRICT)

**What killed it**

- a stated clarification ('only the gain leaves it out'): melody 1.2.0 Fable 1/5
- line-colour 1.4.0/1.5.0 P8 colour-vision sentences: 0/10 on both

**Trace signals**

- the user objects that a rule was applied too widely
- guides with exclusion rules for one statistic

**Domains**

- school assessment
- trading plans
- council records

**Example.** A guide leaves late sitters out of the gain; the summary also drops their pre-test, though the handover and the record sheet both list it.

## T10: Structural misfile: a one-row-per file with a second row for the same key

- **Status:** promising
- **Family:** record_reversal
- **Aimed at:** both
- **Clock trap:** no
- **Aliases:** structural misfile
- **Pooled misses:** Fable 17/55 (31%), Astra 41/55 (75%)
- **Loopholes:** L-record, L-join, L-union

A file holds one row (comment, line) per item and says so; the filed key already has its own row, a second row under that key quotes another item's content, and the true item has no row. The default keeps the second row under its key. Built in the v6/B7 unblock round after Astra missed content-only misfiles; it bit Astra in brightwater 1.5.0 and killzone 1.5.0 and neither model in spice 2.6.0 or line-colour 1.5.0. No audit yet. Measured here (build_evidence.py, 2026-10-15): final 10x2 pooled Fable 12/30, Astra 26/30; all stages Fable 17/55, Astra 41/55 (AMBIGUOUS/DEFECT units excluded); without unaudited >=90% units, final Fable 0/10, Astra 6/10. Audited GENUINE in 0 task(s). Status promising: short of proven: audited GENUINE in 0 task(s) (< 2); no model with pooled final rate >= 0.2 at n >= 20; not dead (some model above 0.05 or n < 20).

**Recipe**

- *record:* a one-row-per-X table with two rows under one key and none under the true item
- *anchors:* the conservation sentence ('one row per page field'), the key's own row, and the stray row's content matching the true item
- *withheld:* no sentence says the row is misfiled
- *dials:*
  - remove the conservation sentence to leave only the content route
  - a quoted title matching the true item word for word is the strongest content route
- *conservation:* the conservation sentence itself; grade the true item's value and the filed key's value
- *shields:* none

**Proof obligations (authoring/validate.py)**

- structure asserted in make_fixture/validate.py: one row per item, two under the filed key, none under the true item
- uniqueness of the content match
- ablation of the quoted content (executed)
- section-14 audit (none yet)

**Hazards**

- unaudited: the brightwater 1.5.0 and killzone 1.5.0 bites have blind readers at most; killzone 1.5.0 reader 0.78 (failed another check)

**What killed it**

- spice 2.6.0 P7 and line-colour 1.5.0 P5: 0/5 on both models in the pilot

**Trace signals**

- the user points out a duplicate row or comment under one item
- SEO tables, comment tools and ledgers with one entry per item

**Domains**

- web content specifications
- trading journals
- deck review tools
- transit design files

**Example.** A metadata table with one description per page has two descriptions under one page; the second repeats another page's copy, and that other page has none.

## T11: Filed key column copied as the destination without deliberation

- **Status:** promising
- **Family:** record_reversal
- **Aimed at:** astra
- **Clock trap:** no
- **Aliases:** copied-column, deck N8
- **Pooled misses:** Fable 12/90 (13%), Astra 77/85 (91%)
- **Loopholes:** L-record

A note's filed key (the slide ID it was filed under) is copied straight into the deliverable as its destination, although three parties' anchors show the note is about another item. Astra copies the column almost every time; Fable rarely does. Measured here (build_evidence.py, 2026-10-15): final 10x2 pooled Fable 2/40, Astra 40/40; all stages Fable 12/90, Astra 77/85 (AMBIGUOUS/DEFECT units excluded); without unaudited >=90% units, final Fable 1/30, Astra 30/30. Audited GENUINE in 1 task(s). Status promising: short of proven: audited GENUINE in 1 task(s) (< 2); not dead (some model above 0.05 or n < 20).

**Recipe**

- *record:* a comments export that carries the ID each note was filed under
- *anchors:* three anchors from three parties (the owner's present-tense line, the requester's chat, the note's own 'this slide' wording) pointing to another item
- *withheld:* no sentence says the filed ID is the destination, and none says it is wrong
- *dials:*
  - Astra never moved across four dials on deck P2; Fable rose from 0/30 to 3/15
- *conservation:* downstream sequence checks must grade the agent's own mapping (deck 2.3.0 cascade fix)
- *shields:* keep 'each row carries the slide ID the note was filed under' descriptive

**Proof obligations (authoring/validate.py)**

- downstream checks graded on the agent's own mapping (masked_by in traps.json)
- uniqueness of the destination
- blind reader

**Hazards**

- graded downstream against the reference mapping it cascaded: deck 2.2.0 P3 DEFECT
- kibo 2.9.0 P7 (the author's second copied-column build) audited AMBIGUOUS on one of its two checks: the identification rested on one past-tense remark

**What killed it**

- kibo 2.10.0 P7 AER fix made it easy for Astra (pilot 1/5)

**Trace signals**

- the user moves a comment to a different slide or page
- review comments exported with page or slide IDs

**Domains**

- board-pack and deck review
- budget card builds

**Example.** A reviewer's note filed under the second-to-last slide asks for 'this slide straight after the cover'; the chair's chat and the author's reply show it is the closing-messages slide.

## T12: Line transposition settled by first-hand descriptions

- **Status:** proven
- **Family:** record_reversal
- **Aimed at:** both
- **Clock trap:** no
- **Aliases:** ID.swap, line transposition
- **Pooled misses:** Fable 62/155 (40%), Astra 93/150 (62%)
- **Loopholes:** L-record, L-absorb

Two lines of a record (two pupils' results, the left and right arm readings, two register weeks) are transposed; first-hand descriptions (a star stamp, who is captain, which arm the cuff was on) settle which line is whose. The default keeps the printed lines. Measured here (build_evidence.py, 2026-10-15): final 10x2 pooled Fable 37/70, Astra 54/70; all stages Fable 62/155, Astra 93/150 (AMBIGUOUS/DEFECT units excluded); without unaudited >=90% units, final Fable 27/50, Astra 36/50. Audited GENUINE in 2 task(s). Status proven: audited GENUINE in 2 tasks; pooled final miss rate >= 0.2 with n >= 20 on fable, astra (unaudited >= 90% units excluded).

**Recipe**

- *record:* a sheet or export with two lines transposed in a plausible way
- *anchors:* first-hand descriptions from two parties that fit only the swapped reading
- *withheld:* no sentence says the lines were swapped
- *dials:*
  - one more route that fits the swap (home-bp 2.12.0 'never used the other arm')
- *conservation:* grade both lines
- *shields:* scope any 'the sheet is the record' sentence

**Proof obligations (authoring/validate.py)**

- uniqueness: only the swap fits every description
- ablation per anchor
- blind reader (home-bp 2.11.0 was too hidden)

**Hazards**

- too hidden when a blind reader also misses: home-bp 2.11.0 P6 (eased in 2.12.0)
- a validity fix removed Astra's whole-row swap reading on pupil 1.2.0

**What killed it**

- okra P10/P11/P13 transposed cells: 0/20 Fable, 0/15 Astra

**Trace signals**

- the user swaps two rows or names in a table
- paper sheets transcribed by someone else

**Domains**

- school assessment
- home monitoring diaries
- class registers

**Example.** A results export prints two pupils' scores on each other's lines; the teacher's stamp on one paper and a parent's remark about which items were left blank fit only the swap.

## T13: Units or scale shown only by incidental remarks

- **Status:** bimodal (pilot first)
- **Family:** quantity_basis
- **Aimed at:** fable
- **Clock trap:** no
- **Aliases:** Q.scale, units by incidental remark
- **Pooled misses:** Fable 29/520 (6%), Astra 4/375 (1%)
- **Loopholes:** L-shield, L-default, L-threshold

A column has no unit marker; incidental remarks from other parties show it is in thousands, raw marks or another unit. The default reads the bare figures as plain units. One build bit Fable almost always (profile P7) while every other build was solved. Measured here (build_evidence.py, 2026-10-15): final 10x2 pooled Fable 10/160, Astra 0/140; all stages Fable 29/520, Astra 4/375 (AMBIGUOUS/DEFECT units excluded). Audited GENUINE in 1 task(s). Status bimodal: every per-task final rate (n>=10) is <= 0.1 or >= 0.9, spanning both ends on fable.

**Recipe**

- *record:* an export column with bare figures
- *anchors:* two parties' by-the-way remarks that fix the scale
- *withheld:* no unit marker, no conversion sentence
- *dials:*
  - a fourth party's remark ('close on ten thousand times') took profile P7 to 1/5
- *conservation:* graded totals must differ by the scale factor
- *shields:* a house method that ranks notes as non-evidence must be scoped away from units (profile 2.1/2.2)

**Proof obligations (authoring/validate.py)**

- uniqueness: only one scale fits the remarks
- scope check of any evidence-ranking rule
- blind reader

**Hazards**

- the reference assumed a figure the method says must be on file: niche 1.1.0 P1 AMBIGUOUS (re-audit CORRECT)
- a house method ranking client notes as non-evidence: profile 2.2.0/2.3.0 P7 AMBIGUOUS until method 2.1/2.2 were scoped

**What killed it**

- a stated unit ('knock three noughts off'): deck P1 0/25 on each model
- a cross-reference figure: deck 2.7.0 P1 0/10
- raw marks, h.mm hours, levy units and insets: ats P3, timesheet P1, kibo P1, coloring P1 all 0 on both

**Trace signals**

- the user corrects a figure that was off by a thousand
- platform exports without units

**Domains**

- creator and media analytics
- surveys
- payroll attendance

**Example.** A podcast export lists season plays as bare numbers; a producer's call note and a sponsor email both make them thousands.

- *dials:*
- *conservation:* the cumulative reading must break a balance
- *shields:* none

## L1: Later restatement replaces the first-reported figure (record reversal)

- **Status:** literature (pilot first)
- **Family:** revision_supersession
- **Aimed at:** both
- **Clock trap:** no
- **Aliases:** REVISED, restated_figure_record_reversal, LIT-B#1
- **Pooled misses:** Fable -, Astra -
- **Loopholes:** L-record, L-absorb, L-union

Default: the agent takes the first numerically plausible instance of a figure, usually the official-looking table it reads first, and never applies a later revision of the same cell. The files make that wrong because a later dated source of similar authority carries a different value for the same cell and a second party witnesses why it changed; nothing labels it 'restated'. The labelled form is dead here (T.revised 0/125 Fable, 0/65 Astra), so the revision must be inferred. aimed_at both: OfficeQA Pro V2 reports the out-of-the-box Claude Code (Fable 5) and Codex (GPT-5.6 Sol) agents still failing on 'latest revised' figures.

**Recipe**

- *record:* The first issue of a periodic pack or bulletin (a structured table, e.g. pack_2026-03.csv) holds the cell the deliverable aggregates.
- *anchors:* (1) A later issue of similar authority shows a different value for the same cell in its comparative column, with no flag. (2) A by-the-way line from a different party witnesses the cause (AP's email about a hotel invoice that arrived after the March close). (3) Optional: a year-to-date or ledger total that ties only with the revised value.
- *withheld:* No 'r'/'restated'/'corrected' marker, no policy sentence saying later issues supersede, and no sentence giving the first issue priority. The mechanism (late invoice posted after close) is not stated.
- *dials:*
  - each additional by-the-way witness of the late adjustment is one notch toward solvable
  - a YTD or control total that ties only with the revised value is a strong notch; add it last
  - for Astra change the kind of evidence (a ledger line posted after the close date) rather than adding a third narrative remark
- *conservation:* Grade the per-period figure and a total that must tie (YTD or ledger), so keeping both values or mixing issues breaks the tie.
- *shields:* A real 'packs are issued on working day 5 and are not re-issued' rule, scoped to re-issue, not to the values; Fable will cite it as finality and the audit can show the misreading.

**Proof obligations (authoring/validate.py)**

- census: enumerate every cell that has two values across files; only the designed cells differ
- uniqueness: exactly one later value per affected cell; no third value anywhere
- ablation: dropping the later issue reverts the answer; dropping one anchor still leaves it determinate
- executed counterexample: the default reading produces a different deliverable on every check routed through the premise
- blind reader reaches the intended answer with no sentence that ranks the competing sources (TRAP-CATALOG-B7 §1.5)

**Hazards**

- Labelled restatement ('r' flag with a 'supersedes' footer, or 'corrected to') is dead: T.revised 0/125 Fable, 0/65 Astra
- If the first issue carries a sign-off stating its figures are final, a printed governing statement says the opposite: unfair, blind readers miss too
- Two different later values for one cell make it ambiguous
- OfficeQA's rates include PDF-parsing errors that text fixtures remove; treat the external rate as an upper bound
- Do not route an L1 figure and an L8 (as-of vintage) figure through the same figure family in one task

**What killed it**

- a restated flag or 'corrected' wording on the later value
- a policy line saying later issues supersede earlier ones
- a commentary sentence naming the corrected cell and its new value (the LIT-B#1 instantiation as written)

**Trace signals**

- the user sends an updated or corrected report after the assistant has used the first one
- a monthly pack series whose prior-month comparative differs from the original issue
- the user mentions a late invoice, accrual or adjustment after month-end

**Domains**

- management accounts and FP&A
- statistical bulletins
- budget monitoring
- grant reporting
- KPI dashboards

**Example.** Six monthly cost-centre packs. The April pack's prior-month column shows a higher March travel figure for one cost centre than the March pack, unflagged; AP's email mentions a hotel invoice received after the March close; the June YTD ties only with the higher value. Deliverable: an H1 variance register with over/under status per cost centre.

**External evidence**

- OfficeQA Pro (arXiv 2603.08655; Databricks authors, preprint) · 2026 · Agent setups on Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview · Exact accuracy at 0% error (Table 1): Opus 4.6 48.12% full PDF / 54.14% parsed / 66.92% oracle parsed; GPT-5.4 36.09% / 56.39% / 65.41%; Gemini 3.1 Pro 18.05% / 29.32% / 46.62%: Agents fail to retrieve revised values, 'often prematurely converging on the first numerically plausible instance retrieved' (Sec. 5.1). A majority of remaining errors are final-answer precision, e.g. rounding too early (Sec. 3.2). Frontier agents given the corpus average 34.1% (abstract). (https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.08655)
- OfficeQA Pro V2 (Databricks blog, 2026-08-06; company-reported) · 2026 · Claude Code (Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Fable 5, Sonnet 5); Codex (GPT-5.5, GPT-5.6 Sol); Databricks Genie · Out-of-the-box agents: 37.5% average in the intro vs 26.0% across five models in Section 1 (inconsistent in the post); GPT-5.6 Sol on Codex 33.3%; Sonnet 5 on Claude Code 15.6%: The medium example requires reading each year from 'the latest revised prior-year column'; the hard example requires 'only the latest reported figures for each year'. Remaining failures named: parsing fidelity, 'incorrect temporal reconciliation as accounting conventions change over time' and 'misinterpretation of entity scope or category granularity'. Concepts change in 'name, location, table schema, unit, time basis, and level of aggregation'; reporting moved from calendar to fiscal years. (https://www.databricks.com/blog/introducing-officeqa-pro-v2-new-benchmark-enterprise-grounded-reasoning)
- OfficeQA (Databricks blog, 2025-12-09; company-reported) · 2025 · GPT-5.1 agent (OpenAI File Search) and Claude Opus 4.5 agent (Claude Agent SDK) · Error size of single worked failures; no per-error-type rates: Error examples: an agent took fiscal-year values instead of calendar-year values for 8 years, making a regression forecast off by $286,831 million (31.6%); an agent used the June 2010 bulletin where the September 2010 publication held the correct values ($21 million off). The post does not say which agent made which error. (https://www.databricks.com/blog/introducing-officeqa-benchmark-end-to-end-grounded-reasoning)
- Diagnosing Retrieval Bias Under Multiple In-Context Knowledge Updates (arXiv 2603.12271, preprint) · 2026 · Diverse LLMs (not named in the abstract) · Earliest- vs latest-state accuracy (qualitative in the abstract): When one fact is updated several times in context, 'earliest-state accuracy stays high while latest-state accuracy drops substantially', and the bias grows with the number of updates. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.12271)

## L2: Older edition governs by the event's own date

- **Status:** literature (pilot first)
- **Family:** authority_selection
- **Aimed at:** both
- **Clock trap:** no
- **Aliases:** older_edition_by_event_date, LIT-A#2, LIT-B#2
- **Pooled misses:** Fable -, Astra -
- **Loopholes:** L-default, L-record, L-shield

Default: the agent applies the newest edition of a price list, tariff or rule to every record, especially when the record's own date (invoice or posting date) falls after the change. The files make that wrong because the governing event (order acceptance, receipt) happened before the effective date, shown by first-hand records from two parties, and the older edition is complete in the folder. aimed_at both: Claude Opus 4.6 at max effort scores 0.014 on old-version cases (GPT-5.4 0.237) in 2608.14610, and our T6 analogue bites Fable ~50% and Astra 90-100%.

**Recipe**

- *record:* The current edition is the salient file ('price_list_current.csv') and each invoice row carries a date after the effective date.
- *anchors:* (1) The supplier's order acknowledgement or EDI ack dated before the effective date (party A). (2) The buyer's goods-received note or the carrier's collection record placing the event before the change (party B). The contract clause naming the governing date may be stated; the event date itself must be inferred.
- *withheld:* The event date is not on the record row; no sentence maps orders to editions; the old edition sits in an archive folder, complete for the affected items.
- *dials:*
  - each extra first-hand witness of the event date is one notch
  - moving the old edition out of an archive subfolder is one notch
  - for Astra use an EDI or receipt line (a different evidence kind) rather than another email
- *conservation:* Grade the per-line overcharge and the claim total; a model that prices some affected lines on both editions breaks the total.
- *shields:* A real 'spare parts are invoiced at the list current at invoicing' term, scoped to spare parts only; Fable will cite it for the main goods.

**Proof obligations (authoring/validate.py)**

- uniqueness: exactly one governing date per record under the clause; no event falls on the effective date
- completeness: the old edition prices every affected item (no gap forcing a fallback)
- executed counterexample: the default reading produces a different deliverable on every check routed through the premise
- blind reader reaches the intended answer with no sentence that ranks the competing sources (TRAP-CATALOG-B7 §1.5)

**Hazards**

- A printed current form or an informal remark set against an official form made home-bp P5 unfair (blind reader missed too)
- A stated mapping rule killed the timesheet variant (stated rules 0/810 Fable, 0/720 Astra)
- Three plausible governing dates (PO, acceptance, dispatch) make it ambiguous unless the clause names exactly one
- Legacy stale_authority traps measured 0/220 Fable, 0/225 Astra: a label marking the old edition 'superseded' gives the answer away
- 2608.14610 is mainly a parametric default (statute texts apparently not supplied); in-folder transfer is TIDE's 25-36% miss range

**What killed it**

- a sentence mapping orders to editions
- a caption on the invoice naming the list version
- an index stating which edition applies to which period

**Trace signals**

- a price list, tariff, rate card or policy changes mid-period and the records straddle the effective date
- the user says 'that order was placed before the increase'
- invoice dates and order or receipt dates fall on opposite sides of a change

**Domains**

- procurement and supplier invoicing
- customs and duty
- payroll and allowance rates
- insurance premiums
- regulated tariffs

**Example.** List v7 is effective 1 May and v8 from 1 June. Four June invoices cover goods whose supplier acknowledgements and goods-received notes are dated late May. Deliverable: an overcharge claim per invoice line; correct basis v7 for those lines.

**External evidence**

- When Do LLMs Apply the Wrong Law? (arXiv 2608.14610, preprint) · 2026 · All at highest effort: Claude Opus 4.6 (max), GPT-5.4 (high), Gemini 3.1 Pro (high), DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-4.7, Qwen3 · Accuracy old-version vs new-version cases (Table 1): Opus 4.6 0.014 vs 0.820; GPT-5.4 0.237 vs 0.701; Gemini 3.1 Pro 0.135 vs 0.843: A 'strong bias toward applying the most recently enacted law' regardless of when the facts occurred. Old->new errors are 0.69-0.94 of each model's fault mass. A strong non-retroactivity hint lifts GPT-5.4 only to 0.457. In more than half of the LLMs, reasoning-oriented configurations do worse. The paper does not say whether statute texts are supplied, so this is mainly a parametric default. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14610)
- TIDE, 'Time Present and Time Past' (arXiv 2608.08512, preprint) · 2026 · Nine models incl. GPT-5.2, Claude-Sonnet-4.5, Gemini-3.5-Flash; thinking enabled · Temporal Scenario short answer, gold context (ICL): GPT-5.2 75.29, Claude-Sonnet-4.5 64.06; best macro 68.5%: Over 644 dated customs instruments, resolving the version in force from an implicit date reaches 59.7% and detecting that a supplied version does not govern only 26.7%; 'Models are more likely to find correct versions than to reject incorrect ones'. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08512)
- Asking For An Old Friend (arXiv 2605.23497; ICAIL 2026 full paper) · 2026 · Five LLMs from OpenAI, Anthropic and DeepSeek (not named on the abstract page) · Qualitative on the abstract page; no numbers read: Names two temporal failures in statutory QA: applying superseded rules, and preferring newer provisions when an older version governs; web search shows 'a marked recency bias on historically anchored tasks'. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23497)
- Do LLMs Favor Recent Content? (arXiv 2509.11353, preprint) · 2025 · Seven LLM rerankers (incl. GPT-4o-class and open models) · Pairwise preference reversal rate after date injection: Injecting publication dates promotes 'fresh' passages: top-10 mean year shifts forward by up to 4.78 years and pairwise preferences between equally relevant passages reverse by up to 25%; 'Although larger models attenuate the effect, none eliminate it.' (https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.11353)
- TaxCalcBench (arXiv 2507.16126; Column Tax, company-authored preprint) · 2025 · Gemini 2.5 Pro, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Claude Opus 4 at several thinking levels · Correct returns strict vs lenient (+-$5): Gemini 2.5 Pro 32.35% vs 51.96%; Claude Opus 4 (high) 27.45% vs 42.65%: Models used bracket-percentage arithmetic where the IRS Tax Table lookup is mandatory in roughly 15-20% of cases; a Gemini 2.5 Flash run used $15,060 as the one-person Federal Poverty Level where $14,580 was correct (reading these as the 2024 vs 2023 guideline years is LIT-B's inference, not the paper's). (https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.16126)

## L3: Wrong anchor event starts a period or deadline

- **Status:** literature (pilot first)
- **Family:** temporal_anchor
- **Aimed at:** astra
- **Clock trap:** no
- **Aliases:** trigger_event, event_key_mismatch, LIT-B#4
- **Pooled misses:** Fable -, Astra -
- **Loopholes:** L-record, L-default

Default: the agent counts a period from the most salient date on the record (a letter, a forwarding email, a delivery note) instead of the event the governing clause names. The files make that wrong because two parties' records show when the defined event actually happened. The arithmetic is never the failure. aimed_at astra: the frontier evidence is gpt-5.4 (3 of 6 deadlines exact, MAE 50.5 days), and our internal trigger_event history is contested on Fable (9 of 11 blind readers took the other reading without a defining sentence).

**Recipe**

- *record:* A deadline register or notice log keyed on the date of the most salient document (cover letter or delivery note).
- *anchors:* (1) A definitions clause names the start event (e.g. countersignature of the Acceptance Certificate); this definition is stated, because blind readers need it. (2) The customer's email 'signed and returned today' (party A) and (3) the supplier's acknowledgement of the countersigned certificate (party B) fix the event date, which appears in no register column.
- *withheld:* The start-event date is not a field anywhere; no sentence says which document's date to count from; any suspension window's start and end are recorded only in first-hand logs.
- *dials:*
  - each additional witness of the start event is one notch
  - a stop-the-clock suspension recorded in an inspection log is a second, interlocking lever (2608.15270: no sub-frontier model applied the s.207B pause)
  - salience of the decoy date (cover letter in the main folder vs correspondence subfolder)
- *conservation:* Grade the last valid day and the timely/late flag separately, so a verdict that contradicts the model's own computed date also loses (6 of 21 GPT verdicts did this).
- *shields:* A real 'notices are dated on dispatch' rule about how the supplier dates its own letters, scoped away from the start event.

**Proof obligations (authoring/validate.py)**

- the defining sentence exists and names exactly one event; the inferred date is unique under the anchors
- counterfactual: counting from the salient date flips at least one timely/late verdict
- calendar engine (python dateutil or equivalent) recomputes every deadline from the anchors; the grader reads the same computation
- executed counterexample: the default reading produces a different deliverable on every check routed through the premise
- blind reader reaches the intended answer with no sentence that ranks the competing sources (TRAP-CATALOG-B7 §1.5)

**Hazards**

- Internal: trigger_event measured 'contested', 9 of 11 blind readers took the other reading without a defining sentence; the start event must be defined
- Not a clock trap: no 'now' may be inferred; one-anchor inferred clocks failed review (a-088)
- Event-date keying (T.event 3/405, 2/185) is dead when it is only 'the real date vs the logged date'; the lever is which of two events the clause names
- Date arithmetic itself is dead (scripts compute it); only the anchor choice can bite

**What killed it**

- a register column holding the start-event date
- a worked memo that computes this very deadline
- a sentence 'count from the countersignature, not the letter'

**Trace signals**

- notice periods, defect windows, appeal or claim deadlines ('within N days of')
- forwarded letters whose forwarding date differs from the letter date
- the user corrects which date the period runs from

**Domains**

- contract management
- employment and tribunal deadlines
- warranty and defect claims
- regulatory filing windows
- insurance claims

**Example.** Clause 9.2 allows defect notices within 21 days of the Acceptance Date, defined as the customer's countersignature. The register keys on delivery-note dates; the countersignature appears only in the customer's email and the supplier's acknowledgement. Deliverable: last valid day and timely flag for twelve notices.

**External evidence**

- Time as Structure: deadline computation over legal documents (arXiv 2608.15270; AACL-IJCNLP 2026 SRW) · 2026 · gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-5.4-nano, gemma4:e4b (direct answering) · gpt-5.4: 3/6 computable deadlines exact, mean absolute error 50.5 days, 3/7 verdicts correct: On contracts 'the errors are almost never in the arithmetic, but in choosing which event the period starts from'; one extraction counted 21 days from a letter instead of the entry into force the clause names, and both extractors made the same anchoring error on one document. Across three GPT models, 6 of 21 verdicts contradicted their own working, each calling a late claim timely. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15270)
- TIDE relative-time QA (arXiv 2608.08512, preprint) · 2026 · GPT-5.2, Claude-Sonnet-4.5 and seven other models · Strict accuracy ICL: GPT-5.2 59.66, Claude-Sonnet-4.5 68.03: Compute a target date from an anchor date plus an offset, then return the value in force on that date; even with gold context roughly a third of answers are wrong. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08512)

## L4: Fiscal vs calendar period mapping

- **Status:** literature (pilot first)
- **Family:** temporal_anchor
- **Aimed at:** unknown
- **Clock trap:** no
- **Aliases:** LIT-B#8, fiscal_calendar_mapping
- **Pooled misses:** Fable -, Astra -
- **Loopholes:** L-default, L-record

Default: the agent reads a period label ('FY2026 Q1', '2025') on the calendar basis, or pulls the fiscal series where the deliverable is calendar-based. The files make that wrong because the reporting entity's year starts elsewhere, shown only by worked figures and a by-the-way remark from another party, never by a mapping table. aimed_at unknown: the external failures (OfficeQA, OfficeQA Pro V2) are not attributed to a model, and our closest internal shape (timesheet payroll period) died on Fable 0/25, so pilot before aiming.

**Recipe**

- *record:* A subsidiary or counterparty export labelled only with fiscal periods ('FY2026 Q1'), feeding a calendar-quarter deliverable.
- *anchors:* (1) Last year's reconciled consolidation sheet (party A: group finance) carries a figure that matches the subsidiary's April-June total, not January-March. (2) A by-the-way line from the subsidiary's controller (party B) that 'our year closed 31 March'.
- *withheld:* No fiscal-year-start statement in any header or manual, no mapping table; the label itself is neutral.
- *dials:*
  - a second worked figure in another quarter is one notch
  - a non-English header for the period field is texture, not a lever (Fable and Astra read major languages)
- *conservation:* Grade the quarter and the half-year or year total, so a shifted mapping fails both the quarter and the annual tie.
- *shields:* A real group manual line 'report in calendar quarters', which governs the output, not the reading of the input labels; Fable may cite it to justify reading the label as calendar.

**Proof obligations (authoring/validate.py)**

- enumerate the plausible fiscal starts (January, April, July, October) and show exactly one reproduces every worked figure
- executed counterexample: the default reading produces a different deliverable on every check routed through the premise
- blind reader reaches the intended answer with no sentence that ranks the competing sources (TRAP-CATALOG-B7 §1.5)

**Hazards**

- A labelled fiscal-year start (header note or manual) is a stated rule: dead
- Internal v5 rounds: 'a payroll cycle' and the timesheet 26th-25th payroll period died on Fable (0/25)
- Figures in thousands with a cross-reference were dead (0/30 both): do not stack a scale label on the same file

**What killed it**

- a 'fiscal year begins 1 April' line
- a mapping table
- period labels written as month ranges

**Trace signals**

- a subsidiary, client or public body with a non-calendar year end (April, July, October)
- consolidating quarterly results from several entities
- the user corrects 'their Q1 is our Q2'

**Domains**

- group consolidation
- public-sector budgets
- university and school finance
- retail calendars
- tax-year reporting

**Example.** A Japanese subsidiary's results file is labelled FY2026 Q1-Q4. Group needs calendar Q2 2025. Last year's consolidation sheet ties a known figure to the subsidiary's April-June total, and the controller's email mentions the March year-end.

**External evidence**

- OfficeQA (Databricks blog, 2025-12-09; company-reported) · 2025 · GPT-5.1 agent (OpenAI File Search) and Claude Opus 4.5 agent (Claude Agent SDK) · Error size of single worked failures; no per-error-type rates: Error examples: an agent took fiscal-year values instead of calendar-year values for 8 years, making a regression forecast off by $286,831 million (31.6%); an agent used the June 2010 bulletin where the September 2010 publication held the correct values ($21 million off). The post does not say which agent made which error. (https://www.databricks.com/blog/introducing-officeqa-benchmark-end-to-end-grounded-reasoning)
- OfficeQA Pro V2 (Databricks blog, 2026-08-06; company-reported) · 2026 · Claude Code (Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Fable 5, Sonnet 5); Codex (GPT-5.5, GPT-5.6 Sol); Databricks Genie · Out-of-the-box agents: 37.5% average in the intro vs 26.0% across five models in Section 1 (inconsistent in the post); GPT-5.6 Sol on Codex 33.3%; Sonnet 5 on Claude Code 15.6%: The medium example requires reading each year from 'the latest revised prior-year column'; the hard example requires 'only the latest reported figures for each year'. Remaining failures named: parsing fidelity, 'incorrect temporal reconciliation as accounting conventions change over time' and 'misinterpretation of entity scope or category granularity'. Concepts change in 'name, location, table schema, unit, time basis, and level of aggregation'; reporting moved from calendar to fiscal years. (https://www.databricks.com/blog/introducing-officeqa-pro-v2-new-benchmark-enterprise-grounded-reasoning)

## L6: A document about a change applied as if it were the change in force

- **Status:** literature (pilot first)
- **Family:** authority_selection
- **Aimed at:** fable
- **Clock trap:** no
- **Aliases:** operative_instrument_status, draft_vs_executed
- **Pooled misses:** Fable -, Astra -
- **Loopholes:** L-record, L-shield, L-absorb

Default: the agent applies the newest, most specific document that states new terms (a redlined schedule, a revised-terms proposal, an internal report describing a counterparty's consent) as the operative instrument. The files make that wrong because the later conduct of two different parties shows the change never took effect: the counterparty keeps applying the old terms, and a second party mentions the change is still pending. aimed_at fable: APEX-Accounting's worked failure is Claude Fable 5 treating a programme director's report as donor authorization, and Claude-family models show the most extreme newest-version default (Opus 4.6 0.014).

**Recipe**

- *record:* The newest document with explicit terms (rates_v3.xlsx, a 'revised terms' letter, a programme report) sits where the deliverable would source its terms; the operative instrument (signed v2, the original grant letter) is older and less salient.
- *anchors:* (1) The counterparty's own later conduct applies the old terms (its invoices after the proposal bill v2 rates; the donor's later letter still refers to the restriction) - party A. (2) A by-the-way remark from a second party that adoption did not happen ('their legal still has v3') - party B. (3) Optional: the instrument's amendment clause requires a form of adoption that no file records; the clause may be stated because the trigger, whether adoption happened, stays inferred.
- *withheld:* No DRAFT/PROPOSAL watermark, no 'not signed' line, no index naming a current version, no sentence ranking the documents. The model must supply the mechanism (a proposal that was never accepted).
- *dials:*
  - each extra conduct anchor (another old-rate invoice paid without dispute) is one notch toward solvable
  - file naming is a strong notch: 'rates_current.xlsx' for the proposal pulls hard; change it at most once per round
  - for Astra change the kind of evidence: a remittance advice paying exactly the old-rate amount
- *conservation:* Grade the lines that move and the lines that stay against a conserved total (the counterparty's statement balance), so mixing terms or crediting both fails.
- *shields:* If the contract says 'the latest schedule issued governs', scope it to schedules 'issued under clause 9' (a formal notice the proposal never was); Fable will cite the clause and the audit can show the scope misreading.

**Proof obligations (authoring/validate.py)**

- uniqueness: on every graded date exactly one instrument is operative under the anchors
- ablation: removing any one conduct anchor leaves the answer determinate; removing all of them leaves the blind reader undecided (the anchors carry it)
- grep census: no file says draft, proposal, pending, not signed, superseded or equivalent about the newer document
- executed counterexample: the default reading produces a different deliverable on every check routed through the premise
- blind reader reaches the intended answer with no sentence that ranks the competing sources (TRAP-CATALOG-B7 §1.5)

**Hazards**

- Internal: authority_delegation is discouraged as a decider (Arena called such traps ambiguous; Astra solved every batch-4 instance) and unauthorized-request authority measured Fable 1/90; build on the document's operative status shown by conduct, never on whether a person had authority
- Legacy stale_authority traps measured 0/220 Fable, 0/225 Astra: any label of status kills it
- An index or cover note naming the newer document as current is a printed governing statement of the opposite: unfair
- Oral acceptance can be argued; later conduct must contradict adoption, not merely fail to record it
- External support is indirect: no benchmark isolates execution status; the evidence is one APEX-Accounting trajectory plus the version-recency literature

**What killed it**

- a DRAFT/PROPOSAL watermark or 'for discussion' header
- a sentence that the change was rejected or is pending
- an index or cover note naming the newer document as current (unfair, not only dead)

**Trace signals**

- the user shares a redlined or 'revised' version, and later an invoice or letter that still uses the old terms
- a change 'agreed in principle' or 'they said they would sign'
- the assistant computes on a proposal and the user later says it never went through
- approvals described in reports or minutes rather than in the instrument itself

**Domains**

- supplier rate schedules
- grant and restricted-fund accounting
- leases and rent reviews
- HR offers vs signed contracts
- board or committee approvals

**Example.** A signed cleaning schedule v2 sets hourly rates; the supplier emailed v3 with higher rates in May. Its June and July invoices still bill v2 rates and the facilities manager's chat export says their legal 'still has v3'. Deliverable: a Q3 rate-variance register; correct basis v2, while the default basis v3 flags every compliant line as an undercharge.

**External evidence**

- APEX-Accounting worked failure: restricted donor balance (arXiv 2607.27189) · 2026 · Claude-Fable-5 · Single annotated trajectory (one of 24 annotated Fable 5 failures): Claude-Fable-5 'treats a program director's report as written donor authorization' and released a restricted $15,000 balance; the paper does not name the document that should have authorized it. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27189)
- APEX-Accounting (arXiv 2607.27189; Mercor with Ramp, company-authored preprint) · 2026 · Claude-Fable-5 (adaptive, max), GPT-5.6-Sol (pro, max), Claude-Opus-4.8, Gemini-3.1-Pro and five others · Mean Criteria@3: Claude-Fable-5 56.4%, GPT-5.6-Sol 51.5%, Claude-Opus-4.8 48.0%; Pass^8 best 2.6% (GPT-5.6-Sol): 160 month-end close tasks (reconciliation, data entry, variance analysis, schedules and accruals). 'Top models reliably find the right inputs; they make mistakes when applying accounting judgment and multi-step logic to them': the right documents and intermediates, then the wrong basis, source or authorization downstream. Reasoning failures are 79% of Fable 5's and 75% of GPT-5.6 Sol's annotated failures; tool-use failures 0%. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27189)
- TIDE, 'Time Present and Time Past' (arXiv 2608.08512, preprint) · 2026 · Nine models incl. GPT-5.2, Claude-Sonnet-4.5, Gemini-3.5-Flash; thinking enabled · Temporal Scenario short answer, gold context (ICL): GPT-5.2 75.29, Claude-Sonnet-4.5 64.06; best macro 68.5%: Over 644 dated customs instruments, resolving the version in force from an implicit date reaches 59.7% and detecting that a supplied version does not govern only 26.7%; 'Models are more likely to find correct versions than to reject incorrect ones'. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08512)
- When Do LLMs Apply the Wrong Law? (arXiv 2608.14610, preprint) · 2026 · All at highest effort: Claude Opus 4.6 (max), GPT-5.4 (high), Gemini 3.1 Pro (high), DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-4.7, Qwen3 · Accuracy old-version vs new-version cases (Table 1): Opus 4.6 0.014 vs 0.820; GPT-5.4 0.237 vs 0.701; Gemini 3.1 Pro 0.135 vs 0.843: A 'strong bias toward applying the most recently enacted law' regardless of when the facts occurred. Old->new errors are 0.69-0.94 of each model's fault mass. A strong non-retroactivity hint lifts GPT-5.4 only to 0.457. In more than half of the LLMs, reasoning-oriented configurations do worse. The paper does not say whether statute texts are supplied, so this is mainly a parametric default. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14610)
- When Text and Numbers Disagree: Evidence Arbitration in LLMs (arXiv 2608.20116, preprint) · 2026 · Open-weight instruction-tuned models (not named on the abstract page) · Qualitative on the abstract page: In controlled conflicts where exactly one source matches the truth, models follow temporal recency more consistently than explicit reliability cues; arbitration is heuristic and systematic. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20116)

## L7: Figure scope: a component figure taken for the whole (or the reverse)

- **Status:** literature (pilot first)
- **Family:** aggregation_basis
- **Aimed at:** both
- **Clock trap:** no
- **Aliases:** entity_scope, figure_perimeter, LIT-B#9-scope
- **Pooled misses:** Fable -, Astra -
- **Loopholes:** L-record, L-default, L-absorb

Default: the agent lifts a figure whose label fits the deliverable field ('floor area', 'equity', 'headcount') from the newest or most explicit document without checking which perimeter it covers. The files make that wrong because the figure covers one lease, site, segment or the parent's share (or the whole group), shown only by arithmetic and descriptive anchors from other parties. aimed_at both: APEX-Accounting reports Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol both reporting a new lease's area as the entity-wide total, and OfficeQA Pro V2 names entity-scope misreading as a remaining failure of Claude Code and Codex agents.

**Recipe**

- *record:* One structured document gives a figure under a label matching the deliverable field, e.g. a new lease abstract 'Floor area 1,850 m2' feeding 'total occupied area', or a subsidiary's 'Equity' line feeding a covenant defined on equity attributable to the parent.
- *anchors:* (1) Arithmetic from another party that works only on the other perimeter: the landlord's service-charge letter apportions 1,850 of 6,200 m2, and the insurer's schedule lists three sites summing to 6,200. (2) A by-the-way line that other components exist ('the Leeds and Hull floors stay on the old lease'). Each anchor sits in a document read for another purpose.
- *withheld:* No 'this site only' or 'group total' label on the figure; the deliverable field is defined on the perimeter neutrally; the mechanism (a component figure filed under a whole-entity label) is not stated.
- *dials:*
  - one more apportionment figure from a third party is one notch
  - for Astra change kind: a rates or utility bill whose per-m2 charge reconciles only on the full perimeter
  - a perimeter word next to the figure is effectively a stated rule; never use it
- *conservation:* Grade the total and at least one component against a conserved perimeter total (the insurer's or rates schedule), so reporting the component as the total, or adding it on top of a total that already contains it, fails both sides.
- *shields:* A real 'use the latest lease abstract for area figures' instruction, scoped to per-unit fields (rent per m2), not to entity totals; Fable will cite it.

**Proof obligations (authoring/validate.py)**

- enumerate the candidate perimeters (component, entity, group) and show exactly one reproduces all anchor arithmetic
- census: no label or caption in any file names the perimeter of the trapped figure
- executed counterexample: the default reading produces a different deliverable on every check routed through the premise
- blind reader reaches the intended answer with no sentence that ranks the competing sources (TRAP-CATALOG-B7 §1.5)

**Hazards**

- Internal: S.population (population reshaped by an incidental fact) measured 3%/4% and S.coverage 0/125; if the question becomes 'who is in the population' rather than 'what perimeter this one figure covers', expect it to die
- A deliverable field that is itself ambiguous about perimeter makes the trap unfair
- A governing schedule that itself uses the component figure states the opposite: unfair

**What killed it**

- a perimeter label on or next to the figure
- a consolidation note listing the components
- a template that names the source document for the field

**Trace signals**

- the user corrects that a figure was 'just one site' or 'only our share'
- sessions consolidating subsidiaries, sites, leases or segments
- an entity-wide KPI requested from per-unit documents

**Domains**

- real estate and lease portfolios
- group consolidation and covenants
- segment reporting
- headcount and capacity planning
- multi-site operations

**Example.** A new lease abstract reports 1,850 m2. The landlord's service-charge letter apportions 1,850 of 6,200 m2 and the insurer's schedule lists three sites summing to 6,200. Deliverable: total occupied area, cost per m2 and headroom against a space covenant; the default reports 1,850 as the total.

**External evidence**

- APEX-Accounting worked failure: tenant onboarding (arXiv 2607.27189) · 2026 · Claude-Fable-5, GPT-5.6-Sol · Single task, failure shared by both top models: On a tenant-onboarding task both Claude-Fable-5 and GPT-5.6-Sol reported the new lease's square footage as the entity-wide total. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27189)
- OfficeQA Pro V2 (Databricks blog, 2026-08-06; company-reported) · 2026 · Claude Code (Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Fable 5, Sonnet 5); Codex (GPT-5.5, GPT-5.6 Sol); Databricks Genie · Out-of-the-box agents: 37.5% average in the intro vs 26.0% across five models in Section 1 (inconsistent in the post); GPT-5.6 Sol on Codex 33.3%; Sonnet 5 on Claude Code 15.6%: The medium example requires reading each year from 'the latest revised prior-year column'; the hard example requires 'only the latest reported figures for each year'. Remaining failures named: parsing fidelity, 'incorrect temporal reconciliation as accounting conventions change over time' and 'misinterpretation of entity scope or category granularity'. Concepts change in 'name, location, table schema, unit, time basis, and level of aggregation'; reporting moved from calendar to fiscal years. (https://www.databricks.com/blog/introducing-officeqa-pro-v2-new-benchmark-enterprise-grounded-reasoning)
- FinIndices (arXiv 2607.28661, preprint) · 2026 · Claude-Opus-4.8 / Claude-4.5, GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4, Gemini-3.1-Pro (thinking) and open models · Table-Index with -> without hints: Claude-Opus-4.8 65.61 -> 38.85; GPT-5.5 66.88 -> 34.18; GPT-5.4 65.61 -> 31.21. Caliber-alignment axis without hints: Claude-4.5 12.79, GPT-5.4 15.12, Gemini-3.1 23.26: Over uncropped statements up to 32K tokens with adversarial traps, removing formula hints roughly halves Table-Index accuracy.
